summary: Show the operator the drafted intake answers and wait for their reply
instructions:
claude drafted these answers from the idea (brief/intake-draft.json):
  idea: A deadpan official handbook for a man who has just retired and is now home all day, and for the wife who now lives with him. The humour is at home: the kitchen he has started 'helping' in, the cupboards he has reorganised, the quick jobs that took a month. Affectionate; the household is the joke too.
  title: The Newly Retired Man's Guide to Being Home All Day
  buyer: His wife, grown-up children, or work colleagues clubbing together for a leaving gift; also bought for his birthday, Christmas or Father's Day.
  recipient: A man in his mid-sixties who has just retired after about 40 years in work and is now at home every day, with energy, opinions and no meetings.
  recognition_trigger: Reorganising the kitchen cupboards 'so they make sense'; re-loading the dishwasher after someone else has loaded it; announcing a 'project' (the shed, the loft, the garage) that is still open in March; following his wife round the supermarket with suggestions; asking 'what are we doing today?' at 7am; keeping a spreadsheet of the bin collection days; still waking at 6:15 for a commute that no longer exists; calling the grandchildren's nursery run 'the logistics'; telling former colleagues on the phone that he is 'busier than ever'; treating the weather forecast as a briefing.
  humour_level: medium
  visual_feel: classic_editorial_caricature
  colour_direction: muted
  print_colour: black_and_white
  cover_style: picture
  main_character: book_factory_invents
  main_character_details: Graham, 66, just retired after 41 years as a regional operations manager, married to Sue, 63, who has run the house the whole time. Two grown-up children and one grandchild, Ellie, 3. Fixed look: reading glasses pushed up on his forehead, a zip-up fleece gilet, and a tape measure clipped to his belt.
  length: 80
  must_include: none
  must_avoid: Anything about money worries, health decline or death; keep it warm, not patronising.

Could not tell from the idea: none

Show the operator this summary once, ask the unclear questions, and ask them to choose the production policy (autonomous, visual_checkpoint or checkpointed; visual_checkpoint is recommended). Never choose it for them. Nothing is complete until they reply. Then record their reply:

  bookfactory intake retired-mans-guide --confirm --by <operator> --policy <their choice> [--set key=value ...]

--set carries their corrections and their answers to the unclear questions. A new draft may replace this one if the idea changes.
